Subject: Nexa model migration: readiness checkpoint & exemption asks

Hi all —

Quick checkpoint ahead of next week's Nexa migration window. They want to move from inference-v1 to inference-v2 (smaller quantized variant) on 2026-09-07. From the discovery call a few things popped up that we need to confirm before we lock the date: 

1) Exemptions: Nexa has a small set of legacy endpoints that rely on exact tokenization behavior; they may request an exemption to run on a pinned v1 instance for 30 days after the cutover. We need SLA/ops clarity and an approval path.

2) Comms: Customer-facing notice, rollback instructions, and a staged canary plan. Who owns the public comms and the in-product banner?

3) Technical blockers: Will KV cache migration or prefix cache behavior require a migration script from us to avoid token mismatches?

I attached a checklist they shared (nexa-migration-checklist.xlsx). Sarah — can you confirm the feature flags you plan to flip on the 7th and whether Nexa expects any downtime for their integration tests?

Proposed short meeting tomorrow 10:30 PT if that helps.

Thanks —
Ben

Ben / team —

Thanks for the context. A few clarifications from product/ops: 

- Exemptions: We can support a short-term exemption (pinned v1) but it requires an SRE-approved isolation plan. Operationally that means: dedicated route, no shared autoscaling with other tenants, and explicit TTL on the exemption (we prefer <= 30 days). I'll need a signed exemption request from Nexa and confirmation of the exact endpoints.

- KV cache: inference-v2 has a slightly different tokenization edge case for blank-leading tokens in older SDK clients (<= v1.2.0). If Nexa is on an older SDK we should either: (a) run a pre-migration conversion of stored prompts or (b) advise them to upgrade the client before cutover. We can create a small migration script to patch known prompt patterns; estimate ~1 dev day to produce and test.

- Canaries: Ops recommends a 48-hour canary (5% traffic -> 20% -> 100%) with automatic fallback to v1 if error rate or RTT exceeds thresholds.

Action items from product: 
- Lauren: draft SRE exemption checklist and isolation steps (ETA 2026-08-27).
- Karthik: confirm routing/fallback capability and whether the control plane can pin routes per-account (ETA 2026-08-26).
- Marissa: draft customer comms and in-product banner copy (ETA 2026-08-28).

Sarah — if you can get the signed exemption request and confirm SDK versions that will help.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Director, Product Operations, Redwood Inference

Thanks — adding infra/serving perspective. 

- Routing/pinning: control plane supports per-account route pins today; we can provision a pinned v1 pool for Nexa. However, pinned pools cannot autoscale with the shared pool without extra capacity reservations — we'll need to agree on a committed baseline or allow limited burst with higher cost.

- Rollback safety: We will keep the KV caches isolated for the pinned instances. Important: if Nexa uses a cached prefix distribution heavily, eviction patterns differ between q8 and q4 quantized variants; we'll monitor cache hit ratio as a signal for regressions.

- Time estimate: one SRE engineer to set up pinned pool + monitoring alerting (2 business days). If we also deliver the migration script Lauren mentioned, add another 1 dev day.

Question for commercial: do we charge for the pinned pool (monthly reserve) during the exemption period, or treat it as a one-off operational credit? I think we should bill, but can offer an operational credit if this is a one-time migration.
